note: Audit of all remaining stock elements (beyond the 28 in stock-element-realism-patch.json v1) that model a real substance. Values cross-checked against D:/The-Powder-Toy/src/simulation/elements/*.cpp (current game defaults) and physical reference data. Two facts (LOXY non-flammability, DESL autoignition range) were confirmed via live WebSearch this session before the session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted; remaining citations rely on well-established reference values from training knowledge and are flagged '(not live-searched this session)' where applicable so they can be spot-checked later.

O2._why: In-game name OXYG (source file O2.cpp, id PT_O2). Real O2 gas thermal conductivity ~26.3 mW/m*K at 300K, same order as N2/Ar, far below metals. Current value 70 sat above the already-patched NBLE (25) and close to HYGN's pre-patch value, breaking the gas heat-conduct ordering the v1 patch established. Lowered to 20 (just under NBLE) to restore CO2(12) < O2(20) < NBLE(25) < WTRV(28) < HYGN(40) monotonic ordering consistent with real gas conductivities. LowTemperature=90K (boils/liquefies to LOXY) already matches real O2 boiling point 90.19K exactly - left untouched. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_thermal_conductivities ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen (not live-searched this session)

CO2._why: Real CO2 gas thermal conductivity ~16.6 mW/m*K at 300K, the LOWEST of the common atmospheric gases (heavier triatomic molecule, slower mean molecular speed) - yet TPT's unpatched value (88) was the HIGHEST of the unpatched gases, backwards from reality. Corrected to 12, below O2(20) and NBLE(25). LowTemperature=194.65K -> DRIC already matches real CO2 sublimation point (194.65K / -78.5C) exactly - left untouched. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_thermal_conductivities (not live-searched this session)

WTRV._why: Steam. Real water-vapor thermal conductivity ~25-30 mW/m*K in the 373-400K range, similar order to other gases, not the 48 currently coded (which sat oddly between NBLE's pre-patch 106 and OIL/other liquids). Lowered to 28, placed just above NBLE(25) and below HYGN(40) since steam's higher molecular speed at temperature gives it slightly better conductivity than heavier noble gases. LowTemperature=371K condensation threshold (2.15K hysteresis gap below WATR's 373K boil point) is a deliberate anti-flicker gap, not a physical error - left untouched. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_thermal_conductivities (not live-searched this session)

LOXY._why: Liquid oxygen. TPT currently sets Flammable=5000 (game max range), meaning LOX self-ignites into FIRE on contact with heat/spark as if it were a fuel. This is physically backwards by a wide margin: LOX is a powerful OXIDIZER, not a fuel - it does not burn itself, it dramatically accelerates the combustion of other flammable materials it contacts. NFPA/CAMEO classify oxygen 3-0-0-OX: 'not flammable, but as an oxidizer it will intensify combustion.' Set Flammable=0 to match gaseous O2's own Flammable=0. HeatConduct lowered 70->50: real LOX thermal conductivity ~0.15 W/m*K (cryogenic liquid, much better conductor than gas-phase O2 but well below mercury's patched 60). HighTemperature=90.1K->O2 already matches real O2 boiling point - untouched. Confirmed via WebSearch this session: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_oxygen ; https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chemical/8967

LN2._why: Liquid nitrogen. Real LN2 thermal conductivity ~0.14 W/m*K at 77K, close to but slightly below LOXY's, so set just under LOXY's corrected value (50) for consistency. LowTemperature=63K->NICE and HighTemperature=77K->none already match real N2 melting (63.15K) and boiling (77.36K) points almost exactly - left untouched; the lack of a gas-phase N2 element in TPT (HighTemperatureTransition=NONE) is an existing game-design gap, not something this audit can fix without inventing a new element id, which the task rules forbid. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_nitrogen (not live-searched this session)

LAVA._why: Molten silicate rock (basalt-like). Typical thermal conductivity of molten/partially molten silicate rock is ~1.5-2.5 W/m*K, the same order of magnitude as solid rock. The already-patched STNE (generic stone) was corrected to HeatConduct=90 in v1; LAVA's unpatched value of 60 put molten rock as a WORSE heat conductor than its own solid precursor, which is backwards (melts increase ionic/convective heat transport). Raised to 90 to match STNE, keeping the solid-to-molten transition heat-conductivity-monotonic. LowTemperature=MAX_TEMP (custom 'check solidification at all temperatures' sentinel) is load-bearing engine logic for the melt/solidify mechanic - left untouched per the no-touch-transition-mechanics rule. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava (not live-searched this session; general volcanology thermal-conductivity range)

DESL._why: Liquid diesel. TPT currently sets HighTemperature=335K (61.85C) as the auto-combust-to-FIRE threshold, i.e. diesel bursts into flame from being merely lukewarm. Real diesel's flash point is around that range but its AUTOIGNITION temperature (spontaneous combustion without external flame/spark, the correct real-world analogue of TPT's simple heat-triggered HighTemperatureTransition) is much higher. Confirmed via WebSearch this session (Physics Factbook / hypertextbook.com): 'Diesel fuel No. 2 ranges from 527 to 558 Kelvin.' Set to the midpoint of that commonly-cited range, 543K (270C), a ~208K / 62% increase - a wide-margin correction. Flammable=2 (very low, matching the well-known fact that diesel is hard to ignite with an open flame/match) was already correct and left untouched. https://hypertextbook.com/facts/2005/EileenTang.shtml

NITR._why: Nitroglycerin. TPT currently sets HighTemperature=673K (400C), identical to gunpowder's ignition point, treating NG as no more heat-sensitive than black powder. This is physically wrong: nitroglycerin is exceptionally thermally unstable compared to other propellants/explosives (this instability is precisely why it historically required stabilization into dynamite). Standard explosives-chemistry references place NG's runaway decomposition/explosive-ignition onset around 200-220C (473-493K), well below black powder's ignition point. Set to 491K (218C), a commonly cited figure, ~182K lower than the current value - a wide-margin correction reflecting NG's outsized heat sensitivity relative to the game's other explosives. Explosive=2/Flammable=1000 relative-scale values (already tied with C-4, above GUN) were left untouched since they are directionally reasonable on TPT's own small internal scale. NOT live-searched this session (WebSearch budget exhausted first) - flagged for a follow-up confirmation pass. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitroglycerin

PLUT._why: Task-specified correction. Real plutonium melting point is 912.5K (639.4C); TPT currently sets HighTemperature=10000 (effectively 'never melts'). Corrected to 913K per task instruction. HighTemperatureTransition intentionally left as NT (unchanged) and all nuclear/fission reaction behavior is untouched, per the rule that PLUT/URAN/DEUT nuclear-fuel gameplay mechanics stay exactly as TPT models them. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plutonium

URAN._why: Task-specified correction. Real uranium melting point is 1405.3K (1132.2C); TPT currently sets HighTemperature=10000 (effectively 'never melts'). Corrected to 1405K per task instruction. HighTemperatureTransition intentionally left as NT (unchanged) and all nuclear/fission reaction behavior is untouched, per the rule that PLUT/URAN/DEUT nuclear-fuel gameplay mechanics stay exactly as TPT models them. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium

RBDM._why: Rubidium. Current Weight=100 places it in the same density tier as gold/tungsten/iron (all Weight=100), but real Rb density is only 1.532 g/cm3 - a light alkali metal, denser than lithium (0.534 g/cm3, patched to Weight=17 in v1) but nowhere near the ~7.9-19.3 g/cm3 of the Weight=100 metals. Interpolating TPT's own weight scale between WATR (1.0 g/cm3 -> 30) and SAND (2.65 g/cm3 -> 90, unchanged/already-correct anchor) gives Rb (1.532 g/cm3) ~= 49; interpolating instead from LITH's already-patched anchor (0.534 g/cm3 -> 17) gives ~49 as well. Two independent anchor pairs converge on ~48-49, vs. the current 100 - more than a 2x overstatement, a wide-margin density error. Melting point (312K, matches real 312.46K almost exactly) and Flammable/Explosive (already near-max, appropriate for a metal that ignites on contact with water/air) were already correct and left untouched. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubidium (not live-searched this session)

skipped.GOLD: already realistic, no wide-margin error. HighTemperature=1337K matches real Au melting point (1337.33K) almost exactly. HeatConduct=251 (max) is close to real Au thermal conductivity 317 W/m*K, near the top of the game's conductivity scale as expected for a precious metal. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold
skipped.WATR: boiling point (373K -> WTRV) and freezing point (273.15K -> ICEI) are already physically correct per task instruction. HeatConduct=29 is lower than real water's ~0.6 W/m*K would suggest on the stated log scale, but water is the single most gameplay-critical liquid in the game (used in nearly every build); this deviation is not a wide-margin error worth risking widespread build breakage over, so left untouched.
skipped.SLTW: already realistic, no wide-margin error. Freezing point 252.05K (-21.1C) matches the real NaCl-water eutectic point almost exactly. Boiling point 383K (109.85C) is close to saturated brine's real boiling point (~381.85K / 108.7C). Weight=35 vs WATR's 30 (~17% denser) matches saturated brine's real ~1.2 g/cm3 vs water's 1.0 g/cm3 reasonably well. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brine
skipped.DSTW: already realistic, no wide-margin error. Freeze/boil points (273.15K/373K) match pure water exactly, as expected (removing dissolved ions does not change water's phase-change temperatures). HeatConduct=23 vs WATR's 29 is a small, gameplay-only differentiation, not a physical error worth touching on a gameplay-critical liquid.
skipped.GUN: Gunpowder ignition threshold HighTemperature=673K (400C) falls within the real, fairly wide literature range for black-powder ignition/deflagration onset (roughly 560-700K depending on composition and confinement); not wrong by a wide margin. Left as the fixed reference point for other explosives per the task's instruction to size explosives relative to TPT's own scale.
skipped.TNT: in-game source file is BANG.cpp (display name TNT). Explosive=0 and Flammable=0 by design - TNT's detonation is implemented via bespoke code elsewhere rather than the generic Flammable/Explosive stats, so it is gameplay-critical/behavior-locked rather than a simple numeric realism issue. Left as the second fixed reference point for the explosives category.
skipped.C-4: in-game source file is PLEX.cpp (display name C-4). Flammable=1000/Explosive=2 already reflect the real-world fact that C4 burns readily from an open flame without detonating (it needs a shock/detonator to explode) while still being rated as TPT's most 'explosive' stat-driven material; not wrong by a wide margin on TPT's own relative scale.
skipped.C-5: fictional material ('cold explosive, set off by anything cold') - has no real-world analogue to audit against.
skipped.THRM: Thermite. HighTemperature=ITH (10000, i.e. does not self-ignite from ambient heat) correctly reflects that real thermite is notoriously hard to ignite by heat alone and normally requires a magnesium starter/very high localized heat - this is already realistic, not a wide-margin error.
skipped.RBDM_note: see patch.RBDM above - melting point and reactivity were already correct; only Weight (density) was corrected.
skipped.BMTL: 'Breakable metal' is a generic gameplay abstraction (a deliberately weaker/lower-melting-point building metal for pressure-based mechanics), not a specific real substance with its own reference data. Its pre-patch HighTemperature (1273K) mirrors METL's own pre-patch value, but raising it to match METL's corrected 1811K would remove the intentional low-melting gameplay niche BMTL exists to fill and could break existing builds that rely on it melting near 1000C; left untouched as gameplay-critical.
